answer: Each identity must prove a 10 Mbps link for 24 hours: three random verifiers send probes each hour, and throughput below 8 Mbps fails it. Bandwidth cannot be cloned like a pearl copied in glass, since one pipe cannot serve two proofs at once without both dropping below the bar; an attacker renting a link per fake pays full price each time, so 100 fakes cost 100 links, not one reused. Like boats queuing at a jetty, each extra fake needs its own berth. Probe logs are signed and on-chain, so any verifier replays the timings like facets of an opal and confirms every pass.
